title: _🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_
body:
_🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**The state block escapes the size cap and can push the comment past GitHub's hard limit.**

`_cap_body` guarantees `body <= MAX_COMMENT_CHARS` (60,000), but `_render_state_block(runs=all_runs)` is concatenated *after* capping. With `MAX_STORED_RUNS = 30`, each run record serializes to roughly 300 chars, so the block can add ~9–10 KB — more than the 5,536-char slack to GitHub's 65,536 limit — and the update/create call then fails with a 422 exactly in the worst case (large review, long-lived PR).

Reserve the state block in the budget before capping:

<details>
<summary>🛠️ Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    body = _cap_body(body=body)
-    return body + _render_state_block(runs=all_runs)
+    state_block = _render_state_block(runs=all_runs)
+    body = _cap_body(body=body, reserved=len(state_block))
+    return body + state_block
```

and thread the reservation through the capping helpers, e.g.:

```python
def _cap_body(*, body: str, reserved: int = 0) -> str:
    limit = MAX_COMMENT_CHARS - reserved
    ...
```
(applying `limit` in `_elide_low_value_sections`, `_cap_findings_section`, and the final tail truncation instead of the module constant).
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the
rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate.

In `@lintro/ai/review/github_sticky.py` around lines 91 - 110, Reserve the
rendered state-block length before applying the comment size cap so the final
concatenated comment remains within MAX_COMMENT_CHARS. Update _cap_body to
accept a reserved-size parameter and use the reduced limit throughout
_elide_low_value_sections, _cap_findings_section, and final truncation; call it
with the length of _render_state_block(runs=all_runs), then append the state
block unchanged.
```

</details>

_🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**First-match marker lookup lets untrusted finding text hijack the parsed state.**

Model-derived text is only sanitized for `@mentions`, so a finding body can embed ``. Since the real block is always appended last, searching from the end makes the parse unspoofable.

<details>
<summary>🛡️ Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    start = body.find(STATE_MARKER_PREFIX)
+    start = body.rfind(STATE_MARKER_PREFIX)
     if start < 0:
         return []
```
</details>



<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
    start = body.rfind(STATE_MARKER_PREFIX)
    if start < 0:
        return []
    after = body[start + len(STATE_MARKER_PREFIX) :]
    end = after.rfind(STATE_MARKER_SUFFIX)
    raw = after[:end] if end >= 0 else after
```

</details>
